regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, and graphical reaction summary
regions.finding: The title/abstract and generic reaction drawing summarize CuCl-mediated carbomagnesiation/carboxylation of 2,3-allenols with R4MgCl and a CO2 balloon, with an overall 58–93% range. This is classified as a general overview, not an individual batch.

regions.region: page 1 two-column introduction and lower-right prior-work/proposed-route prose
regions.finding: Prior alkynol/Grignard/CO2 literature and the authors' earlier iodination work are literature context. The proposed cyclic intermediate A and lactonization concept continue in Scheme 1 on page 2; no page-1 experiment beyond later table rows is created.

unresolved: The graphical summary uses generic R groups and does not assign its yield range to a unique experiment.
No Supporting Information file was supplied or explicitly associated.

regions.region: page 2 upper-left Scheme 1 and adjacent optimization prose
regions.finding: Scheme 1 combines a prior-work iodination branch with a proposed CO2 capture/lactonization branch. It is retained as a general scheme, while the prose is linked to Table 1 rows rather than duplicated.

regions.region: page 2 left-center Table 1 reaction drawing, entries 1–5, and footnotes a–c
regions.finding: Five independent optimization experiments were retained with halide/additive identity, additive equivalents, two-stage conditions, substrate/CuCl/Grignard/ether quantities, NMR yields, and the separate 87% isolated yield in entry 5.

regions.region: page 2 upper-right Table 2 reaction drawing, entries 1–5, and footnotes a–d
regions.finding: Five halide-comparison experiments were retained separately: bromide entries 1/3 have NMR yields, chloride entries 2/4 give 72%/78%, and iodide entry 5 is reported only as complicated after 24 h.

regions.region: page 2 lower-right Table 3 reaction drawing, entries 1–14, and footnotes a–b
regions.finding: Fourteen substrate-scope experiments were retained row-by-row with R-group labels, Grignard identity, time, and isolated yield. Entry 12 is a distinct 7 mmol (1.12 g) scale-up and is not merged with entry 11.

unresolved: Most table rows omit atmosphere, exact warming profile, acid identity, workup, purification, and isolated masses.
The entry-12 scale-up does not print scaled reagent/solvent quantities.
Complex product structures and stereochemistry remain machine-unverified; SI is unassociated.

regions.region: page 3 upper-left continuation of Table 3 discussion
regions.finding: The 7 mmol Table 3 entry 12 result is reiterated. A distinct 1c/3 equiv n-C4H9MgCl/24 h comparison is reported only as giving a lower yield of 2ca; the numerical yield is preserved as missing. Premature protonation is mentioned only as an unassigned minor byproduct in some cases and is not assigned to a fabricated row.

regions.region: page 3 left-center Scheme 2, four optically active substrate/product arrows
regions.finding: Four independent chirality-transfer experiments were retained with substrate/product configurations, starting and product ee, row-specific first-stage times, and yields 70–93%. The acknowledgment that (S)-2na was reproduced is supporting context, not a duplicate experiment.

regions.region: page 3 upper-right Scheme 3, two R rows from chloropropargylic alcohol 3
regions.finding: Two distinct one-pot experiments were retained: R=H to 2ea (10 h, 67%) and R=Ph to 2aa (13 h, 51%), with 6 equiv n-BuMgCl, 2 equiv CuCl, CO2 balloon, and 1 M HCl workup.

regions.region: page 3 conclusion, acknowledgments, Supporting Information statement, and references
regions.finding: The conclusion summarizes the chloride effect. Reproduction statements for 2cb, 2ma, and (S)-2na were linked to existing records. The article says SI exists online, but no SI file is supplied or explicitly associated here; references were not expanded into current-paper experiments.

unresolved: The lower-yield 3-equiv comparison has no numerical yield or fully restated conditions.
The premature-protonation byproduct is not assigned to specific rows or a structure.
Scheme 2 omits scale, workup details, yield basis, and ee method; Scheme 3 omits scale, solvent volume, purification, and yield basis.
Supporting Information remains unassociated and all complex structures/configurations need review.
